title: Point it at a drive or folder
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

This slice creates the scanner, but it is labelled risk tier low. The project's process constraint says scanner slices are cut at a higher tier and that the lightest process cannot tell which ones those are. Should the engine re-tier SL-020 so the counting rules get the harder review?

Is it acceptable for the build to run Microsoft's dotnet-install.ps1 into a gitignored .dotnet/ when no 10.0 SDK is present? If not, someone with admin installs a 10.0 SDK machine-wide once, and eng/dotnet.ps1 becomes a check with no install.
Code-behind only in the window versus a view-model. This is fine for one window, but the next slice (the tree) will add screens and may want the opposite.

The optional path argument as a supported CLI contract versus a test-only hook. It is kept as a contract because validate drives a real drive with it, and it also gives 'pick a folder' a scriptable route.
One Core assembly holding Native, Scanning and Store versus splitting the store into its own project. It is one project now, and the internal write API is what keeps the seam.

Ten test classes plus a fixture for the first slice. This is heavier than the lightest process would pick, but the project constraint requires the five counting-rule tests before any scanner slice can pass.
Path\.GetFullPath-only-in-LongPath.cs architecture rule (in O-003's fix text). The person's decision on M2 took only the interop rule, so it was not added.
The Win32Path type and ScanStore.GetNativePath (O-003). They are deferred by the decision to the slice that adds a third Win32 caller.
A display accessor that follows a hardlink duplicate to its charged record (O-002). It is deferred by the decision to the tree slice.
--fail-skips (O-007). It is deferred by the decision until an actual move to xUnit v3; the project is on 2.9.3.
Counting large-file disagreements 'with WSL running' (O-004 fix text). WSL was not running and I did not start a VM on the owner's machine, so the C: count (964 probed, 0 disagreeing) is without WSL.

A C: scan makes 259,041 probes (about 7.5% of 3.4M files), almost all of them WOF suspects and first hardlink repeats (WinSxS). The large-file rule added only 964. The design's premise that probes are rare does not hold on this PC, although the scan still took 61.7 s warm and 71.1 s through the app. The cold-scan cost of the probes is worth measuring.

The large-file rule makes pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys fail their probe (error 32, sharing violation) on every C: scan, so the Finished note always counts at least these. Their listing values are correct. A later slice may want to treat a sharing violation on paging files as expected rather than as a probe failure.
%TEMP%\fsa-guard-tests holds cloud-tagged leftover files from another project's tests (error 363 when probed). They are not this repo's and were not touched.

ChargedSize reads HardlinkDuplicate, which the scanner sets just after Append. A reader during a scan (the tree slice) could briefly see a duplicate as charged. Setting the flag before the count is published would close that.
m7 (deferred by the person): CancelSynchronousIo for a network or cloud call that blocks, with 995 handled as cancellation. It still needs a later slice that hardens network and cloud volumes.

O-013's explanation of the coverage gap (NTFS metafiles, a breakdown of the unreadable folders) belongs to the coverage-panel slice. The registered read-denied-folders operation can measure how much of the 50.7 GB the 599 unreadable folders hold.
The engine's stored design for SL-020 still carries the pre-amendment text. The design-slice stage may want to take docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md into its record.

caused_by.reason: 1 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-004), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-004 (fix): M3 (major): The design treats a stale directory listing as a hardlink problem and a WOF problem only. It trusts the listing's EndOfFile and AllocationSize for every other file. NTFS caches these values in the directory entry and refreshes them only on close, so a file held open and growing during a scan can report an old size. Such files are large: WSL and Docker .vhdx disks, VM disks, databases,… C…
